lp.structure_note: Unlike a general partnership (partnership.json), an LP IS a filed entity: it requires a Certificate of Formation with the Secretary of State (Form 207, governed by Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 1 Ch. 3 Subchapter A and Title 4 Chapters 151/153) and a registered agent, and it IS subject to Texas franchise tax regardless of partner composition (Tex. Tax Code Section 171.0002(a) lists 'limited partnership' directly -- there is no natural-person-ownership exception here the way there is for general partnerships under Section 171.0002(b)(2)). CONFIRMED 2026-08-30: an LP has two genuinely different partner classes with different liability exposure. General partners have the same unlimited, joint-and-several liability as in a plain general partnership. Limited partners are NOT liable for LP obligations (Section 153.102) UNLESS they either also serve as a general partner, or participate in control of the business beyond simply exercising their rights as a limited partner -- Section 153.103 provides a long statutory safe-harbor list of activities (being an employee/agent/contractor, consulting/advising, voting on specified fundamental matters, guaranteeing obligations, and others) that do NOT count as 'participating in control.' An LP may also elect to register as an LLP on top of its LP status (an 'LLLP') -- this is an optional upgrade, not this file's default state, and triggers an additional annual report to the Secretary of State by June 1 each year (Section 152.806) on top of the standard PIR.

identity: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status
Initial General and Limited Partners List
Statement Required for Liability Protection (if applicable -- good-faith erroneous limited-partner-status cure)
governance: Limited Partner Voting Records (per Partnership Agreement)
Limited Partner Safe-Harbor Activity Log (documents which activities a limited partner has undertaken, to preserve liability protection)
financial: Federal Partnership Tax Return (Form 1065) and Partner K-1s
statutory: Texas Business Organizations Code Chapters 151 and 153 Compliance
Texas Franchise Tax Public Information Report (PIR) Filing
Foreign Qualification Filings (if operating in other states)
LLLP Election Consideration (optional LLP registration stacked on top of the LP -- triggers an additional June 1 annual report to the Secretary of State)

Certificate of Formation (Limited Partne: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 1, Chapter 3, Subchapter A (general formation) and Title 4, Chapters 151 (general partnership provisions applicable by reference) and 153 (LP-specific provisions) -- filed via Secretary of State Form 207. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 207 instructions.
Statement Required for Liability Protect: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 153.106 (protection for a person who erroneously but in good faith believed they had become a limited partner) and Section 153.107 (the statement that must be filed with the Secretary of State to preserve that protection, within a defined time limit after discovering the mistake).
Limited Partner Safe-Harbor Activity Log: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 153.102 (a limited partner is not liable for LP obligations unless also a general partner or participating in control of the business) and Section 153.103 (a lengthy, non-exclusive statutory list of activities -- including serving as an employee, agent, or contractor of the LP or a general partner; consulting/advising; voting on specified fundamental matters; guaranteeing obligations; and others -- that do NOT count as 'participating in control').
Franchise Tax Filings: Tex. Tax Code Section 171.0002(a) explicitly lists 'limited partnership' as a taxable entity. Unlike a general partnership (which is exempt if owned entirely by natural persons, per Section 171.0002(b)(2)), an LP has no such exception -- franchise tax and PIR filings apply regardless of partner composition. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 via the Texas Comptroller's own franchise tax publications.
LLLP Election Consideration (optional LL: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 152.801/152.802 (LLP registration, applied to an LP by reference) and Section 152.806 (a Texas LP that also registers as an LLP must file an additional annual report with the Secretary of State no later than June 1 each year -- on top of, not instead of, the standard PIR filed with the Comptroller). CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 207 instructions.
Registered Agent Designation: Standard Texas registered-agent requirement -- an LP cannot act as its own registered agent, and the registered agent must have affirmatively consented to serve, per the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 207 instructions.
